entry: Sergey Levine, Peter Pastor, Alex Krizhevsky, and Deirdre Quillen. Learning hand-eye coordination for robotic grasping with deep learning and large-scale data collection, 2016. URL https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.02199.
contexts: Current methods can be broadly categorized into teleoperation-based techniques [51, 16, 47, 42], vision-driven demonstrations [3, 26], and sensor-enhanced interfaces [6, 40, 48].
reasoning:
We need to decide if reference [26] supports FastUMI's use. FastUMI sentence: "Current methods can be broadly categorized into teleoperation-based techniques [51, 16, 47, 42], vision-driven demonstrations [3, 26], and sensor-enhanced interfaces [6, 40, 48]."

So they cite [26] as an example of "vision-driven demonstrations". The cited paper is Levine et al. 2016 "Learning Hand-Eye Coordination for Robotic Grasping with Deep Learning and Large-Scale Data Collection". Is that a vision-driven demonstration? It is a learning-based approach using monocular images to servo grasping, i.e., vision-driven grasping. It is not a teleoperation demonstration, but a vision-driven method. So it supports the categorization as vision-driven demonstration. The claim: FastUMI relies on [26] as an example of vision-driven demonstration methods. The paper indeed presents a vision-driven grasping method using deep learning from monocular images. So supported.

That indicates vision-driven. Or "Our approach ... uses a deep convolutional neural network to determine how likely a given motion is to produce a successful grasp, and a continuous servoing mechanism that uses the CNN to continuously update the robot’s motor commands."
